precepts.text: The fear of the Lord goeth before the obtaining of authority, but roughness and pride is the losing thereof. You rule people with roughness and pride, you going to lose your position. We just had a case like that in Cali; we have many cases in the states, New York, Texas, where brothers felt, in order to be a leader of the sanctuary, I got to rule the people with roughness and pride, and they was taking advantage of the brothers and sisters out there. No, we had to remove you.
precepts.point: King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died., you came in to collect money? We ain't giving you nothing. And Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot to flee to Jerusalem; he said, they going to kill me next. So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“And the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the old men’s counsel”. Sirach tells what that does: “The fear of the Lord goeth before the obtaining of authority: but roughness and pride is the losing thereof.” You rule people with roughness and pride, you are going to lose your position.

That is what happened to Rehoboam. The ten tribes said “What portion have we in David?” “to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David.” When he sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, all Israel stoned him to death: you came to collect money? We are not giving you anything. Rehoboam made speed to get up to his chariot and flee to Jerusalem, thinking they would kill him next. “So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.”

We just had a case like that in Cali, and many cases in the states, New York and Texas, where brothers felt that in order to be the leader of the sanctuary they had to rule the people with roughness and pride, and they were taking advantage of the brothers and sisters. No: we had to remove you. Roughness and pride is the losing of authority.

precepts.text: The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker. For pride is the beginning of sin: it is the beginning of you falling to your temptation, falling to your lust, falling to feed that appetite; because you knew better, you had all the warning signs, you were given a way out as we read in 1 Corinthians 10, but pride overcame you and your mind was not on the Lord when your back was against the wall. And he that hath it shall pour out abomination: and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities. When that pride overtakes you, the Lord adds to your demise and leaves you to Satan, because your mind is not right.
precepts.point: Pride. Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall. You think you know it all, you think you have all the wisdom and understanding; but pride is the progenitor of your destruction, because pride removes correction. You do not want to hear it. Pride isolates you, and pride precedes the collapse.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
“Pride goeth before destruction”. Where does pride begin? Sirach: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That means you have a froward mind.

“For pride is the beginning of sin”: the beginning of you falling to sin, falling for your temptation, falling to your lust, falling to feed that appetite. You knew better. You had all the warning signs, all the opportunity, everything placed in front of you. You were given a way out, as 1 Corinthians 10:13 said: God will with the temptation make a way to escape. But pride overcame you. Your mind wasn't on the Lord when your back was against the wall.

“and he that hath it shall pour out abomination”. When you have that pride, a negro is unstoppable; a prideful negro, oh my God. “and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.” When pride overtakes you, the Lord adds things to your demise: I'm going to leave you to Satan to gobble you on up, because your mind ain't right; you're too prideful.

That is why pride goes before destruction. Pride removes correction; you don't want to hear it. You think you know it all, you have all the wisdom and understanding. Pride isolates you, and it precedes the collapse.

precepts.text: As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers. Take the young men in regular clothes six months in the truth: they are going to follow the example of the officers that have been here eight, nine, ten years. If you are bashful, afraid, timid, and shy, your spirit is telling those brothers it is okay to be like this. It shall not be so in here.
precepts.point: This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, it spreads to the soldiers under him.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

precepts.why:
“And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” He was scared. This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, what is that going to do to the soldiers under him? It is going to spread.

“As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers”: so are they that are under him. “And what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” Whatever man the ruler is, like King Saul, such are all that dwell under him.

Take an example. Some brothers have been here six months, a year maybe, not long, still in regular clothes. Some officers have been here eight, nine, ten years. Those young men in the regular shirts are going to follow the example of the officers in the purple shirts. So if you are bashful, afraid, timid and shy, what does that communicate to them spiritually? That they can be timid, shy, fearful and bashful too. You don’t have to say nothing; your spirit is telling them, it’s okay to be like this, the officer can be fearful and timid, so I’ll follow his example, now I know how to move around in here.

It shall not be so. It shall not be so in here.

precepts.text: The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God.
precepts.point: I will take away out of the midst of thee them that rejoice in thy pride: the pastors and the parties rejoice in us going against God's commandments.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.why:
Zephaniah says, “for then I will take away out of the midst of thee them that rejoice in thy pride”. Who rejoices in our pride? Sirach proves what pride is: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God”.

Pride is departing from God, going against his commandments; it is our sin. So those that rejoice in our pride are the ones that rejoice in us going against God's commandments: the pastors, the Christians, the churches, the Democrats and the Republicans. They rejoice in us not keeping God's commandments. The Lord says, I am going to take them out of you, take them away from you, “and thou shalt no more be haughty because of my holy mountain”, the land of Israel.

What he leaves is “an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of the Lord.” The elect beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, the daughter of his dispersed, a large portion of them on the continent of Africa, are afflicted and very poor, as we saw going throughout Africa keeping Passover and the feast of unleavened bread. They must be taught to trust in the name of the Lord.

“The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies”, because they are being taught the commandments, and that is what we go out there for. No, Jesus is not white; no, he was not born December 25th; no, we are not to pray to Mary or to the ancestors. Sin has always been the problem, and breaking God's commandments is a sign of unbelief. When the ones who rejoice in our departing from God are taken away, the remnant shall feed and lie down, and none shall make them afraid.

precepts.text: The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God and his heart is turned away from his maker: that is the pride of life.
precepts.point: Brothers, a sister in pants should infuriate you, not catch your eye; the Lord of Israel is the belt doing the whipping now, and it will continue as long as our people love this kingdom.

note.label: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.why:
John says “all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” The lust of the flesh: in America everything is accessible; order it and it's there in twenty minutes. The lust of the eyes: social media, looking at the big butt, keeping up with the Joneses, twerking, the competition of niggardom: I can jump on a car better than she can, I can roll a blunt this big, I can rap about nothing and can't say my ABCs. Our people love the world for those things but fail to love God.

And what is the pride of life? Sirach answers: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That is the pride of life we just read in 1 John. It is when you hate God and retract yourself from the love of the heavenly Father, when you prefer this world, this system and this setup over the guidelines of God, and would rather have this phobia of freedom and be guided by your oppressors.

The scriptures say pride goeth before destruction. When you go contrary to the Lord, death is at your door: “For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that hath it shall pour out abomination: and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.”

Your heart is then removed from the one that created you. “And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof”: Esau's rulership is already ordained to pass away. Will you escape when the destruction comes, or pass away with it?

precepts.text: A wise judge will instruct his people; as the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers. Disorganized camps that talk about rape and build nothing reflect their leaders. When we go to Chicago we are on O'Block teaching, not filmed eating chicken and pizza in the hood at midnight.
precepts.point: Any task set before our forefathers got done: the Maccabees who were not warriors, the slaves who left Egypt. Egypt was America. If the shooting starts, we know scripturally what happens; the Lord takes care of it.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
“A wise judge will instruct his people; and the government of a prudent man is well ordered. As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” However the leader is, that is how the men under him are going to be.

So when you see these other camps that look disorganized, that are talking about rape, that have not built anything in years, find their leaders, and that is what you will see. When you see us traveling all over the world, building institutions, organizations within the organization, look at our leaders. We are the representation of our leadership.

When we go to Chicago we are not on film eating chicken and pizza in the hood at midnight. How is that a leader of a congregation? You will never see a bishop or a deacon put out a video like that. When we went to Chicago, we went to O’Block teaching the word of the Lord.

Everything rises and falls on leadership. There are cities where the leader was changed and the camp took off, and other places where the leader left and everything fell apart. You are who your leader is. That is why everybody wants to ask the Bishop for the secret sauce, but what they do not understand is that Christ is at the head and we are all following Christ. The Most High is building 144,000 leaders, sealed with the law of God, and nothing they try can stop it.

That is why the people of Nehemiah had a mind to work: the wall reflects the ones leading the building.

precepts.text: The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker. When your study habits change and you pull back from the believers, pride has set in and you are regressing.
precepts.point: The kingdom is like leaven a woman hid in three measures of meal till the whole was leavened. Leaven grows.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
This tends to happen every year around the Passover, and this is a call to wake some up so they can get their mind right. “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God”. When you notice that your study habits have changed, when you notice that you're pulling back from the believers, understand that pride has now set in. You are regressing, going backwards.

“and his heart is turned away from his Maker”. That sin, that leaven, is now blinding you, so that you can no longer see clearly. That is the leaven spreading through the whole lump: it starts small, with a pulling back, and grows until the heart is turned away from the Most High.

precepts.text: Why is earth and ashes proud? There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man, for such an one setteth his own soul to sale, because while he liveth he casteth away his bowels. Oprah did not get all that money for being a great host, and the athletes did not get those contracts just for talent.
precepts.point: Revelation 18:3: all nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath of her fornication, the same wine of Habakkuk 2:5, her policies; the kings of the earth, presidents and prime ministers, committed fornication with her, and the merchants waxed rich through her delicacies.

note.label: War & the Pain of Repentance

precepts.why:
“And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her; for no man buyeth their merchandise any more”. The merchants are the corporations that make major deals with countries. The gold, silver and precious stones come this way by ship in those big containers, and the majority of what is listed comes from the continent of Africa. Then: “and slaves”: that was you and me. “And souls of men”: you want a piece of the pie, you have to sell your soul. There are things you must do.

Ecclesiasticus says it: “Why is earth and ashes proud?” Earth and ashes represents man; why is man proud? “There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man”. They covet what does not belong to them. If you are covetous, you want a piece of the American pie, those billions of dollars in contracts. “For such an one setteth his own soul to sale; because while he liveth he casteth away his bowels.” While he lives he casts away his bowels, the lower intestine, the rectum.

You think Oprah got all that money just because she was a great talk show host? You think LeBron and these athletes got those contracts because nobody is as good as them? Michael Jai White is a good actor, but there are certain things he said he is not going to do, so he does not get those contracts. Ye said, if you see a video of me with a goat, because he knew what they held over him. They have something on all of them. The model from our Houston school, the Black Starlet who found a line of producers at the door: to get the contract you cast away your bowels.

That is why Paul says “they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.” Covetousness is the last of the ten commandments, and it starts in the mind; covet and you will steal, steal and you will lie, and it goes on to murder. The fear that keeps them from repenting is being publicly humiliated for what they did to get their fortunes, the way they destroyed Wendy Williams. But the Lord can still preserve the soul: come out of that lifestyle.

precepts.text: It is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves. Nobody consulted us about where to put the knee or what colour skin to give us.
precepts.point: Pride is hateful before God and man. You can repent and hop back to the right side, but on the side of pride you are on the side God hates, and everything he hates has an expiration date.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“Pride was not made for men, nor furious anger for them that are born of a woman.” Pride, arrogance, disdain, the inability to admit fault, the inflated ego: God said it wasn't made for you. You are nothing but dust that shall return to where it came from. And anger doesn't get you anywhere either; it holds you back and stunts your growth.

Why wasn't pride made for us? “Know ye that the Lord he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves”. You didn't put one finger on your hand. You didn't put the knee bone with the hip bone and the leg bone. All of that belongs to God, the Creator, from way back when he said, Let us make man in our image.

He didn't consult you: where should I put the knee? How high up on the leg should it go? What should the arch of the foot look like? What skin tone should I give them? What should I make their hair like? None of us were included in that conversation.

So pride has no ground to stand on. The one who did not make himself cannot be proud before the one who made him. That is why the beginning of pride is turning away from your Maker.

precepts.text: Thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb; thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all. Science explains what God allows, then tries to outdo him by altering the body.
precepts.point: Pride is hateful before God and man. You can repent and hop back to the right side, but on the side of pride you are on the side God hates, and everything he hates has an expiration date.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit”: you don't know how the spirit was even made, and the body doesn't function without a spirit in it. We say someone is soulless, and it may be jacked up and crooked like the Esau in them, but that body isn't walking around with nothing in it. This is not a movie where they clone you and you come back with no soul, or a vampire who lives forever and can't see his reflection. There is a spirit in all of us, and the Most High made that.

“nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child”. Science tries to explain it the best way it can, by the mitochondria and this and that, but they don't know what God did to make it. Science is God giving man some sense of his mastery, and man takes it and says, I can do better than God: let me put this rod on you as a woman, let me cut yours off. That's why the Bible warns us to beware of science that opposes God.

“even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.” So why is earth and ashes proud? Man does not even know how he himself was made; pride was not made for men.

precepts.text: The dust shall return to the earth as it was, and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.
precepts.point: Pride is hateful before God and man. You can repent and hop back to the right side, but on the side of pride you are on the side God hates, and everything he hates has an expiration date.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
Solomon mentions that spirit again: “Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

The body goes back to the dust it came from, and the spirit goes back to God who made it. All of this, the dust and the spirit, belongs to the Most High God. That is why pride is not made for us.

Sirach asks, “Why is earth and ashes proud?” and says that when a man is dead “he shall inherit creeping things, beasts, and worms.” The man who is today a king tomorrow shall die. Neither the body nor the spirit is ours to boast in: one returns to the earth, the other to its Maker. So the beginning of pride, departing from God and turning the heart away from the Maker, is turning away from the very one the spirit must return to.

precepts.text: Ye are bought with a price: glorify God in your body and spirit, which are God's. You are still his child at forty-seven; you do not tell him what you will do with that body.
precepts.point: Pride is hateful before God and man. You can repent and hop back to the right side, but on the side of pride you are on the side God hates, and everything he hates has an expiration date.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” That is who your body belongs to.

This isn't something the young ones usually fight with. It's us, as we get older, who start smelling ourselves: I'm going to do this, this is what I want to do. We forget that at the end of the day we are still the children of the Most High God. You don't get to tell him what you are going to do with that body. The way parents look at their son and say, you'll always be my baby, even at forty-seven with gray hair: apply that to your life with God.

You have to keep these commandments, because he is still your Father and that is what he said to do. And that is the beginning of pride in Sirach 10: “when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” As we get older we start thinking we can decide whether to serve God or obey our Father, and that is pride. Pride is the beginning of sin; don't tell yourself you have a good heart while you depart from his commandments. Pride is hateful before God, and what he hates has an expiration date.

precepts.text: The pride of life is a heart turned away from its maker; pride begins when a man departs from God.
precepts.point: Our views are extreme, meaning the polar opposite of the world. It takes fortitude to take the peer pressure at school and say I am not joining it.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

precepts.text: Elders were ordained in every city to set in order the things that are wanting. The structure, the rank and the processes behind them are what make a government well ordered.
precepts.point: A congregation that is not growing is not a camp-spot problem — ask whether that school is run prudently. When leadership is prudent, cities grow: in understanding, in operations, in the kind of problems that get put behind you.

note.label: To Whom Much Is Given: The Burden and Beauty of Godly Leadership

precepts.text: There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man; he sets his own soul to sale.
precepts.point: To covet is to carry the spirit of jealousy and envy, and there is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: he sets his own soul to sale, selling out his dignity and self-respect to fulfil his desires no matter what it takes.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: for such an one setteth his own soul to sale”. That is Achan. He saw the goodly Babylonish garment, the silver and the wedge of gold among the spoils, coveted them and took them, though they were consecrated unto the Lord for his treasury, so he was stealing from the Most High himself.

A covetous man sells out his dignity and self-respect to fulfil his desires no matter what it takes; he sets his own soul to sale. Achan sold his for a garment and some metal hid in the earth in the midst of his tent. Covetousness carries the spirit of jealousy and envy, and the Lord counted it weighty enough to close the ten commandments with it.

precepts.text: If the ruler is a coward, so goes the rest of the nation; that is why the leader must be fearless, because the hearts of the people depend upon their leadership.
precepts.point: Nehemiah shows the right spirit. In the Persian captivity he had liberty from the king to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, and the enemies Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem plotted to scare him off the work. A hired man urged him to hide in the temple because they were coming to slay him, and Nehemiah refused; operating in the spirit of fear is sin according to the scripture.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

precepts.why:
“As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” If the ruler is a coward, so goes the rest of the nation.

That is why the leader must be fearless: the hearts of the people depend upon their leadership. Nehemiah understood it and would not flee. In Saul’s camp, “all the people followed him trembling.”

precepts.text: That is exactly what happened: Saul's heart turned from his Maker, he poured out sin upon sin from there, and the Lord cast down the proud prince's throne and set up the meek in his stead; that is the whole story we are about to read.
precepts.point: And it grieved Samuel, and he cried unto the Lord all night. Pride had to be in operation for Saul to transgress on that level, and pride is where the throne is lost.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
“It repenteth me that I have set up Saul to be king: for he is turned back from following me, and hath not performed my commandments.” Mark the language: Saul did most of what was said, yet the Lord counts it as turning back and not performing his commandments at all. For everybody who says, well, I did do this part: whenever there is a but in your obedience, you did not perform the orders given unto you.

“And it grieved Samuel; and he cried unto the Lord all night.” Pride had to be in operation for Saul to transgress on that level, and pride is where the throne is lost: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker. For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that hath it shall pour out abomination: and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly. The Lord hath cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.”

That is exactly what happened. Saul’s heart turned from his Maker, he poured out sin upon sin from there, and the Lord cast down the proud prince’s throne and set up the meek in his stead. That is the whole story that follows.

precepts.text: As the ruler is, so are his people, and the power of the earth is in the hand of the Most High, who sets over it one that is profitable in due time.
precepts.point: The power of the earth is in the hand of the Most High, and in due time he sets over it one that is profitable. When Israel will not rule in righteousness, he raises a Nebuchadnezzar; Israel's purpose was never to be wicked and rule at the same time.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

precepts.why:
“A wise judge will instruct his people; and the government of a prudent man is well ordered. As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein. An unwise king destroyeth his people”. As the ruler is, so are his people.

Jehoiakim “did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord his God”, and he destroyed his people. “Against him came up Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and bound him in fetters, to carry him to Babylon.” Nebuchadnezzar “also carried of the vessels of the house of the Lord to Babylon, and put them in his temple at Babylon.”

“The power of the earth is in the hand of the Lord, and in due time he will set over it one that is profitable.” The Most High set a wicked king over the land because his own people would not do what he said. When Israel will not rule in righteousness, he raises a Nebuchadnezzar. Israel’s purpose was never to be wicked and rule at the same time.

precepts.text: As Christ was, so were his officers; the disciples took on his characteristics.
precepts.point: Peter was fearless and intrepid, a man who drew a sword and cut off the man's ear, which was not the first time he used it; he came from the streets, and we have brothers with that same posture. They took knowledge the disciples had been with Christ because you take on the attributes and characteristics of whoever you surround yourself with, and the disciples all spoke the same thing as Christ.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
“As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” As Christ was, so were his officers.

You take on the attributes and characteristics of whoever you surround yourself with. Peter was fearless and intrepid, a man who drew a sword and cut off the man's ear, and that was not the first time he used it; he came from the streets, and we have brothers with that same posture. The rulers took knowledge that the disciples had been with Jesus because they carried his characteristics.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 15 The Seven Last Plagues

precepts.why: What does the Bible say pride is? “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” If you have a problem with your brother, the law says go to your brother; when someone says I’m not doing what the Bible says, I have another way, that’s pride. “For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that hath it shall pour out abomination”: listen to the evil that comes out of the men and women who have pride: pay me, give me my business, you don’t have to keep the Passover anymore.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 15 The Seven Last Plagues

precepts.why: There is nothing worse than a covetous man. “Why is earth and ashes proud?” Earth and ashes is us, mankind. “There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: for such an one setteth his own soul to sale”: you will sell your own soul when you’re covetous. “Because while he liveth he casteth away his bowels”: you will give up your body for what you want, for fame or money.

points: So the Bible says, for you leaders, the fear of the Lord goeth before you obtain authority. Before you get a position, you have to have some fear, a healthy fear of God. Come on.

But roughness and pride is the losing thereof. But being a lord over the flock, when you're hurting the flock, you're quenching the spirit of the flock, is what? The losing thereof. Y'all understand that? So your job is not to lord over, intimidate. What's some good words, y'all? Huh? Be a dictator. No, no, no. A tyrant. That's the word. You're not supposed to be a tyrant over here. The people ain't supposed to necessarily fear you. They're supposed to respect you. Y'all with me? Jump to verse 25.

note.label: From Negroes to Gods from Earth to Gold

points: Unto the servant, or leader, that is wise shall they that are free do service. Meaning they're going to willingly follow you. They're going to willingly be able to serve great men. Come on.

And he that hath knowledge will not grudge when he is reformed. What does that part mean in context? What we talking about? I'll give you an example to keep the class moving. Oh, you go ahead. Afro right there. Young man.
Daniel: Shalom, Cap. Daniel. YOV is saying, when he's corrected, he won't have a grudge or take it personal.

Give him a hand. Give him a hand. You will be surprised at when leadership goes and visits a school, or visits here or visits there, and the leader of the school will get in their feelings. Well, that was wrong, and I don't agree necessarily, and blah blah blah blah blah. Take the correction and move the hell on. Just shut up. Just take the correction. It's what the leadership sees. If you see something different, it is what it is. You understand? But take the correction. Yes, sir. I will fix it. And move the hell on, because you want the correction. Watch this. Proverbs 6:23. A leader that can't take correction, that is a dangerous spirit there. But watch what the Bible says right here.

note.label: From Negroes to Gods from Earth to Gold

points: That's what the Bible says. That's the type of pride it's talking about. When you're too proud to be corrected, that's a devil. And I know a lot of sisters have that spirit right there. Sisters, see, think about it. A sister will not even correct another sister for fear that it's going to turn into an argument. Am I right, sisters? So is it safe to say, "Y'all know y'all crazy. Y'all know y'all crazy, right?" Yes, y'all crazy. Yes. That is an evil spirit, y'all. You understand? If somebody come to you with a scripture and say, "Hey, hey, hey, brother, according to this, you ain't supposed to be doing that or moving that way," and here you go bucking. You're not bucking against me. You're bucking against the word of God. It's not my word. I just brought it to you because I saw it. Y'all with me? Read it again.

The Bible says the beginning of your pride is when one departs from God, and his heart is turned away from his maker. That's a dangerous spirit, a dangerous position to be in right there. Now go back to First Peter 5. First Peter 5, verse 5. Come on.

note.label: From Negroes to Gods from Earth to Gold

points: Now, as a leader, guess what? Some leaders get brought up. And what happens? Some leaders get what? Brought down, right? So, and that is a part of the journey. That is a part of being a leader, you know? So watch this.

Now, roughness and pride is the losing of that position, because you're harming the people one way or the other. Right? So now let's say you fixed that issue. You've been examined. You've been examining yourself. You see the errors in your ways. Galatians 6:1. Come on.

note.label: From Negroes to Gods from Earth to Gold

points: As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers. So if the leadership is weak in your particular camp, how is the men and women under the leadership going to be? Weak. Okay. So you could always judge the leadership based on the brothers and sisters in the body, in the congregation, how they move. If they move reckless, guess what that means? That means you brothers are weak. If they move in order and you know what's going on, guess what that means? Okay, I could work with this leadership here. These brothers are putting forth fruit meet for repentance. Y'all with me now? Give me... I got to speed this up. Hebrews 12:14 through 17. I'm going to try to speed this up a little bit. We got half an hour left.

note.label: From Negroes to Gods from Earth to Gold

points: Just to show you that what Cap is saying is actually biblical, because like you said, the brother is clearly telling you why he came in the building, to get a position. But that is not what we are here for.

The fear of the Lord goeth before the obtaining of authority. Right. So what Cap is saying is Bible. That is what the Lord says. The main objective is to come in here to get your spirit right. That is what we are all here for. And in the doing so, eventually the Lord will put you in a position that you need to be in.

And ultimately you want rank so you can do what? Why does he want rank? So he can be over somebody. I can tell somebody what to do. The scripture says pray for more labourers. That is what it says. Pray for more labourers to do the work. He is praying for rank.

points: A wise judge will instruct his people; and the government of a prudent man is well ordered. A wise judge will instruct his people concerning what? The laws of God. And the government of a prudent man is ordered based on how it is written.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein. A wise judge will instruct the people, and a wise judge will make officers just like him. So if you are a judge and you are in here cursing people out, if you are stealing, if you are dealing foul, you are going to raise a flock of that. That is why you see some of these camps we talked about, they all act the same exact way, the same mentality, because they followed their leader.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: An unwise king destroyeth his people; but through the prudence of them which are in authority, the city shall be inhabited. An unwise leader will destroy the people. The city is going to be inhabited, the congregation is going to grow, if you have a prudent leader, a leader that stands for the laws of God.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: Among brethren he that is chief is honourable; so are they that fear the Lord in his eyes. Among brethren, he that is the chief man is an honourable man. I will use Bishop as the example: he is a chief around here, and it says he is honourable. But look what it says next, so are they that fear the Lord in his eyes. He has to see that these men are honourable also. That is called respect.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: The fear of the Lord goeth before the obtaining of authority: but roughness and pride is the losing thereof. You have to fear God to obtain authority, so you can instruct the people. But roughness and pride is the losing thereof, concerning how you are dealing with the people, because those people you are dealing with are called of God. God called them.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: Great men, and judges, and potentates, shall be honoured; yet is there none of them greater than he that feareth the Lord. Potentates means leaders. You can have great men, but none is greater than the man that fears the Lord. It did not say where he stands in a body. He could be the new man walking in the door, but if he has the fear of the Lord he is greater than those men, if those men do not fear God.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: Unto the servant that is wise shall they that are free do service: and he that hath knowledge will not grudge when he is reformed. Unto the servant that is wise, they that are free shall do service: the people serving him will freely serve him because of his wisdom.

And he that hath knowledge will not grudge when he is reformed. That is going into correction. Correction has to happen, and that helps us grow. He that has knowledge will not grudge when he is corrected and has to change. No excuses. You will accept it, you can respect it.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: Better is he that laboureth, and aboundeth in all things, than he that boasteth himself, and wanteth bread. Remember we are talking about a wise judge. Better to work and build and abound in all things than to boast of yourself as a leader and lack the things you need. It is better to work.

No man as a leader should be in a situation where people are taking care of you. No. The Bible says if a man does not work, he does not eat. By the sweat of your brow you shall eat bread. That is just what it is. You lose the trust of the people, you lose the respect of the people. Imagine a nation of men that do not work and their wives take care of them. That is a camp. There is a camp that does that. Imagine a camp full of unemployed men. Your wife leaving twenty dollars on the night table for you before she goes to work.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: Why is earth and ashes proud? There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man. When you covetous, what you going to do? For such a one setteth his own soul to sale. So you sell your soul. And that's what our people have done in the Christian church.
Because while he liveth he casteth away his bowels. He give up his insides. That's what it mean. You going to sell yourself if you covetous. You get diddified. You become a Diddyite.

You all hear that? So that's why, when Wall Street go belly up, all your money going to go belly up. So you're living under an illusion, man. I'm telling you all, y'all better open your eyes and see what's going on.

note.label: Economic Collapse & Uncertain Riches

points: As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers. There are those who stay silent about their wicked leaders, and silence means you accept it. You want to know why you can't break down the scriptures precept upon precept, and you give foolish breakdowns like John the Baptist was evil and turned against Christ? Because your wicked leaders don't teach and are not keeping the scriptures.

Their mind has become spiritually dark: void of judgment, void of discernment, void of truth. And that spirit spreads like osmosis throughout all the officers and soldiers in the camp. You utter the same rhetoric as your leader, and you can't break down the scriptures, giving breakdowns like wormwood is a drink. Foolish breakdowns, because you're not moving in the spirit; you're moving in the flesh.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: Bear not hatred to thy neighbour for every wrong; and do nothing at all by injurious practices: remember, a bitter person's perception is negative; they cannot see right because they want to abide in darkness. The brother is bringing solutions and advice, and they do not see it; they just want to see the brother hurt, the sister hurt, slumped down and aching.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: Pride is hateful before God and man: and by both doth one commit iniquity: with the bitter spirit comes pride, and when you commit iniquity you put yourself out of the kingdom of God.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God. When you pull God out of the equation, the only thing left for you is pride, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that hath it shall pour out abomination. That is why everything coming out of his mouth and his page is abominable, stupid thing after stupid thing every day, and he explains his own logic for all of it.

Therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities: and that is what you are seeing. A war that was supposed to be over in a week has run over a month, and the counselors who said leave those people alone are watching it backfire.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: Pride is hateful before God and man: God hates it and man hates it. When you meet somebody prideful, even though you do not say it, you feel it.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: Because of unrighteous dealings, injuries, and riches got by deceit, the kingdom is translated from one people to another. The riches gotten by deceit was enslaving the children of Israel; almost all these countries were established on the blood, sweat, and tears of slaves. That is why all the kingdoms of the earth are going to lose their dominion, and the one kingdom that will stand is the kingdom of the twelve tribes of Israel.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: For pride is the beginning of sin. That is what pushed her over. Do not ever think a woman does not have pride: that pride is wanting to be over you, to make the decisions. It is what she battles every day, and it runs into sin. He that hath it shall pour out abomination: resentment, grudges, hatred every time you come to correct it. Therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly. Do not let that pride seep into your house.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

points: Pride is hateful before God and man. You can repent and hop back to the right side, but on the side of pride you are on the side God hates, and everything he hates has an expiration date.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

points: The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God and his heart is turned away from his Maker; pride is the beginning of sin. As we grow up we start thinking we can decide whether to serve our Father; that is pride. Anyone who departs from God's commandments is walking in sin, whatever he tells himself about having a good heart.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

points: Pride was not made for men, nor furious anger for them that are born of a woman. You did not make one bone of your own body.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

points: A wise judge will instruct his people; and the government of a prudent man is well ordered. Now, which one of us has a government? Which one of our people has a government? Something about this sovereign thing is that it is always one individual here, one individual there. Unity is not something that the black man has learned to do. There is a group called IUIC that has learned to do that, under the banner and in the wisdom and instruction of God's government. However, the black community is not able to do that. And that is why we always see these foolish individuals proclaiming sovereignty as a slave.

note.label: Sovereign Idiocracy

points: As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein. Now, for starters, to be sovereign you must be a government. You must have a government, and you must have the means to support that government. Otherwise, what are you sovereign from, or to? It makes no sense.

note.label: Sovereign Idiocracy

points: An unwise king destroyeth his people. So it says an unwise king destroyeth his people.

But through the prudence of them which are in authority the city shall be inhabited. Prudence means wise. So through the wisdom of the leader, the people of the city shall be wise. What we are reading about is rulership. What we are reading about is when we once ruled. Or, in the case that we become rulers, as we will, not if but when, in the future.

note.label: Sovereign Idiocracy

points: The power of the earth is in the hand of the Lord. So if the power of the earth is in the hand of the Lord, who is actually sovereign? Only the Lord. There has not reigned a king, whether it be in Israel or otherwise, who is not given that authority by God. That is the reason we are getting this here. There is a reason and a point to that being established. God is who establishes sovereignty, power, authority, control over his earth. And ultimately over his children, the blacks, the Hispanics and Native Americans, so-called, who are the Israelites.
And in due time. Meaning when he feels like it, when he sees fit, to whom he sees fit.
He will set over it one that is profitable. He will set over it one that is profitable. He will.

note.label: Sovereign Idiocracy
